note: Neither game ended. Both used the full 120 s with a stack only 2-3 rows high and no holes, so the score was limited by how fast pieces get placed, not by play quality. About 1280 of the 1875 decisions went to soft-dropping, and steering cost 128 ms per column or turn (64 ms press plus 64 ms release) with Down let go the whole time. The piece now keeps falling fast while it steers: new actions hold Down together with Left, Right, X or Z, and a new slack field allows this only when there are enough free rows along the piece's path. tickMs is halved to 32 so a press and release take 64 ms. A keyReady field replaces the old release logic and retries presses the game ignored. Two guards cover the untested key combinations: if combined presses keep failing they are switched off for the rest of the game, and fallStalled lets go of Down and presses it again if an aligned piece stops falling. No failure windows were saved, so there were no windows to write regression tests against.
instructions: Tetris: every piece is steered to a landing spot the state has already chosen (scored on landing height, rows cleared, holes, wells and transitions, with a look at the next piece). The stack stays low and a game lasts 120 s, so rows cleared depend on how fast pieces are placed: keep Down held whenever there is room. Fields: turnsCW / turnsCCW = X / Z presses still needed for the target orientation; shift = columns still to move (negative = left); aligned = true when turnsCW and shift are both 0. A steering key acts once per press and must be let go for one decision before it acts again: keyReady is false when the last key must be let go now. slack is 'ok' when the free rows under the piece along its whole path are enough to keep holding Down while finishing the remaining turns and shifts, 'tight' otherwise. fallStalled is true when an aligned piece has stopped falling although Down should be held (Down must be let go once so it can be pressed again). turnFits tells whether the next turn fits where the piece is; freeLeft / freeRight are the free columns on each side; pieceCol is the piece's leftmost column. Rules, in order: 1) playing false -> start. 2) piece null -> none. 3) aligned -> none if fallStalled, else drop. 4) keyReady false -> drop if slack is 'ok', else none. 5) turnsCW > 0 and turnFits: if turnsCCW < turnsCW turn with Z (drop_ccw if slack is 'ok', else rotate_ccw), otherwise turn with X (drop_cw if slack is 'ok', else rotate_cw). 6) Otherwise choose a side: left if shift < 0, right if shift > 0; if shift is 0 (a turn is needed but does not fit here) right when pieceCol < 4, else left. If the chosen side is blocked (freeLeft is 0 going left, freeRight is 0 going right), take the other side only while a turn is still needed and that side is free; if no side remains -> drop. 7) Going left: drop_left if slack is 'ok', else left. Going right: drop_right if slack is 'ok', else right. planLines and planHoles describe the chosen landing; rowsToLand is how far the piece can still fall; height and holes describe the stack.

actions.description: release all keys; the piece keeps falling at normal speed
press Left arrow only (Down released): shift the piece one column left
press Right arrow only (Down released): shift the piece one column right
press X only (Down released): rotate the piece clockwise once
press Z only (Down released): rotate the piece counter-clockwise once
hold Down only (steering keys released): the piece falls fast
keep Down held and press Left: shift one column left while falling fast
keep Down held and press Right: shift one column right while falling fast
keep Down held and press X: rotate clockwise once while falling fast
keep Down held and press Z: rotate counter-clockwise once while falling fast
click the game centre to start or restart when no game is on
